name: Senapati Pradyumna Keshari/ସେନାପତି ପ୍ରଦ୍ୟୁମ୍ନ କେଶରୀ

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Senapati Pradyumna Keshari is an Odia poet whom Kabita Live’s biography identifies as a retired teacher of Odia. In an essay for the Goethe-Institut, poet Ashutosh Parida places him among writers attentive to local life and its often overlooked subjects. Odisha’s government library-selection record also lists his poetry collection “Papatrushna”, published by Prabaha in 2008.

His poems here show how far that attention can travel. “Taua” finds endurance and generosity in a blackened cooking griddle, connecting household labour with a speaker’s childhood memories. “Bali Kankada” uses the disappearing sand crab to consider uncertain intimacy, including the distance between a person and their social-media image. “Suryamukhi” turns the sunflower’s devotion towards a landscape of war, where a wounded country’s hope of renewal resists the claims of an occupying power.
